A.subject: Chemistry
A.text:
An organic compound A has only H, C and O. Compound A give red solid on reaction with 2, 4 D.N.P reagent. A react with OH⁻/Δ to give B as one of product

Then most probable structure of A can be
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Solution:

The solution shows a reaction mechanism where:

- Starting compound A contains CH₃ — C(=O) — CH — (CH₂)ₙ — C(=O) — H with an enolate intermediate
- This undergoes intramolecular cyclization via enolate attack on the aldehyde carbonyl
- Forms an intermediate with OH group and ketone on cyclohexene ring
- Upon base treatment (OH⁻/Δ), loses water to form the final product B: a cyclohexene ring with acetyl group (C(=O)CH₃) attached

The key points are:
1. Compound A gives red precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent, indicating presence of carbonyl group(s)
2. The structure must contain both an aldehyde and a ketone to undergo aldol condensation
3. The intramolecular aldol condensation under basic conditions produces the cyclohexene derivative shown as product B

B.text:
Let there be three independent events E₁, E₂ and E₃. The probability that only E₁ occurs is α, only E₂ occurs is β and only E₃ occurs is γ. Let 'p' denote the probability of none of events occurs that satisfies the equations (α − 2β)p = αβ and (β − 3γ)p = 2βγ. All the given probabilities are assumed to lie in the interval (0, 1).

Then, Probability of occurrence of E₁ / Probability of occurrence of E₃ is equal to _______.
B.sol_text:
Let p(E₁) = x, p(E₂) = y and p(E₃) = z

α = p(E₁ ∩ Ē₂ ∩ Ē₃) = p(E₁) · p(Ē₂) p(Ē₃)
⇒ α = x(1−y)(1−z) ...(i)

Similarly
β = (1−x).y(1−z) ...(ii)
γ = (1−x)(1−y).z ...(iii)
p = (1−x)(1−y)(1−z) ...(iv)

(i) and (iv) ⇒ (1−x)/x = p/α ⇒ x = α/(α+p)

(iii) and (iv) ⇒ (1−z)/z = p/γ ⇒ z = γ/(γ+p)

p(E₁)/p(E₃) = x/z = (α/(α+p))/(γ/(γ+p)) = (α(γ+p))/(γ(α+p)) = (1+p/γ)/(1+p/α) ...(v)

Given that
(α−2β)p = αβ ⇒ αp = (α+2β)β ...(vi)
(β−3γ)p = 2βγ ⇒ 3γp = (p−2γ)β ...(vii)

(vi) and (vii) ⇒ α/(3γ) = (α+2p)/(p−2γ)
⇒ pα − 6 pγ = 5αγ
p/γ − α = 5
p/γ + 1 = 6(p/α + 1) ...(viii)

(v) and (viii) ⇒ p(E₁)/p(E₃) = 6
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let L = 0 be a common normal to the circle C ≡ x² + y² - 2ax - 36 = 0 and the curve S ≡ (1 + x)^y + e^(xy) = y drawn at a point x = 0 on S, then the value of r - a, where r is radius of circle, is equal to _______.
B.sol_text:
Given curve is S ≡ (1 + x)^y + e^(xy) = y ...(1)
Put x = 0 in equation (1)
(1 + 0)^y + e^0 = y
⇒ 1 + 1 = y
⇒ y = 2
∴ Any point on curve S is (0,2) when x = 0
Again differentiating both sides of (1), we get
(1 + x)^y (y·(1/(1+x)) + log(1 + x)·(dy/dx)) + e^(xy)(x·(dy/dx) + y × 1) = dy/dx
⇒ (1 + x)^y ((y/(1+x)) + log(1 + x)·y') + e^(xy)(xy' + y) = y'
Put x = 0
(1 + 0)^y ((2/(1+0)) + log(1 + 0)·y'(0)) + e^0(0·y' + 2) = y'(0)
⇒ 1·(2/1 + 0·y'(0)) + e^0(0 + 2) = y'(0)
⇒ y'(0) = 4
Slope of normal at (0,2) = -1/(y'(0)) = -1/4
∴ Equation of normal at (0,2) to the curve is y - 2 = -1/4(x - 0)
⇒ x + 4y - 8 = ...(2)
⇒ L ≡ x + 4y - 8 = 0 is also the normal to the circle
C ≡ x² + y² - 2ax - 36 = 0 ...(3)
∴ Normal (2) will pass through its centre (a,0)
∴ a + 0 - 8 = 0 ⇒ a = 8
Also radius of circle (3) is r = √((−a)² + 0 − (−36)) = √(8² + 36) = √(64 + 36) = 10
∴ r - a = 10 - 8 = 2
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
